post.text:
ZOOM IN. 🔍

The last 24 hours in transhumanism:
- Hera's first close-ups of the crater DART left on an asteroid
- Noticing nature linked to a more meaningful life
- Shark Bay dolphins with steady friends lived longer
- An OpenAI model claims faster matrix maths (preprint)
post.alt: A 3-minute video recap of the last 24 hours in transhumanism (26 Nov 2026): Hera's close-ups of the crater DART left on an asteroid, nature and meaning in life, OpenAI's matrix multiplication claim, DeepMind's self-experimenting agents, an AI-traced 1808 sketchbook, a dish model for longer-lasting brain implants, Alzheimer's mini-brains in space, brain ageing vs dementia in mice, warm nights and memory in Australians, Shark Bay's long-lived dolphins, psilocybin for veterans' anxiety, a Perth site for a psilocybin PTSD trial, AI agents failing everyday chores, New York's AI toy ban, SpaceX's million-satellite licence, XPeng's IRON humanoid and Earth's departing mini-moon, with captions, sources and screenshots of the articles.

stories.title: ESA's Hera sends the first close-ups of the crater NASA's DART left on an asteroid
stories.summary: Hera's first images show DART's 2022 impact left a crater the size of a sports stadium across the whole width of Dimorphos, and set the asteroid tumbling. It's a real-world check on asteroid deflection, a way to protect Earth; closer images come in December.

stories.title: Noticing nature goes with a more meaningful life, Texas A&M surveys find
stories.summary: Across five surveys of more than 1,800 people, appreciating your surroundings was the part of nature most tied to life feeling meaningful, and a short nature video lifted it too. Mostly surveys, so an association: how you spend time outside may matter more than how long.

stories.title: An unreleased OpenAI model claims matrix multiplication's exponent is 9/4
stories.summary: OpenAI's maths repository, 730 manuscripts produced by an unreleased model, claims two big matrices can in theory be multiplied in about n^2.25 steps, below the best published bound of 2.371. It's a preprint mathematicians have yet to check, with no practical speed-up yet.

predictions.note: An unreleased OpenAI model produced 730 maths manuscripts from about 4,000 problems, including a claimed 9/4 matrix bound; preprints not yet checked.

stories.title: DeepMind says AI agents now run some of their own experiments for the next Gemini
stories.summary: Google DeepMind's VP of Research Koray Kavukcuoglu says AI agents control part of the compute to run experiments for upcoming Gemini models, while full recursive self-improvement is still far off. The agents' reasoning isn't rewarded in training, so it stays readable.

predictions.note: DeepMind says AI agents now run some experiments for its next Gemini models themselves, while full self-improvement remains far off: one lab's account.

stories.title: A historian says GPT-6.2 Astra traced an anonymous 1808 sketchbook's likely artist in 22 minutes
stories.summary: Mark Humphries of Wilfrid Laurier University says OpenAI's model named the vicomte de Chabot as the likely artist of a sketchbook at Yale's Beinecke Library; Chabot's diary, which he checked on microfilm, matched the dates and a sketched view. Yale hasn't confirmed.

stories.title: Melbourne scientists recreate brain-implant scarring in a dish, to design longer-lasting implants
stories.summary: A University of Melbourne model combines brain cells with blood immune cells to mimic the scarring that dulls brain implants over time, and an anti-inflammatory calmed it. It's a lab-dish screen for brain-computer interface designs before animal studies.

stories.title: Alzheimer's mini-brains that spent 40 days in space changed differently depending on their genes
stories.summary: UC San Diego sent lab-grown brain organoids carrying inherited Alzheimer's mutations to the space station: each mutation responded in its own way, and a stress protein linked to long life in bowhead whales, CIRBP, rose in all. A small, preliminary lab study.

stories.title: In mice, brain ageing and neurodegeneration start alike, then split as DNA damage builds
stories.summary: Skoltech mapped how DNA folds in mouse neurons: normal ageing and an Alzheimer's-like disease share early changes, but in disease the structure breaks down further as DNA damage accumulates. Slowing ageing and treating dementia may need different drugs.

stories.title: Warmer nights linked to poorer memory in middle-aged and older Australians
stories.summary: In 1,873 Australians aged 42 to 75 tested over several years, warmer overnight temperatures went with lower scores on one of 12 tests: associative memory, the kind that remembers where your keys are. It's an association; disrupted sleep is one possible reason.

stories.title: Shark Bay dolphins with a steady social circle lived longer, 40 years of data show
stories.summary: University of Queensland researchers followed 400 wild dolphins in Western Australia's Shark Bay over 40 years: those consistent in the group size they liked did better, and some lived to 53. It's an association, in dolphins.

stories.title: One psilocybin dose eased anxiety for a year in 15 veterans with hard-to-treat depression
stories.summary: In a small trial without a placebo group, one 25 mg dose of psilocybin, the magic-mushroom compound, given with therapy cut anxiety 59% at three weeks in veterans with treatment-resistant depression, and it stayed lower for 12 months.

stories.title: A Perth clinic joins Compass Pathways' global psilocybin trial for PTSD
stories.summary: Emyria's Empax Centre in Leederville will be a site for Compass Pathways' Phase 2b/3 trial of its synthetic psilocybin for PTSD: about 300 adults worldwide, double-blind, judged at week 8. Recruitment is targeted for December, subject to ethics approval.

stories.title: Even the best AI agents fail over a third of everyday personal tasks, a new benchmark finds
stories.summary: ShellBench, built from more than 10 million real agent interactions, found top models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta failed more than a third of the time, and 15.7% of attempts broke a safety rule, such as missing a child's school pickup.

stories.title: New York bans AI chatbot toys for five years
stories.summary: Governor Kathy Hochul signed a five-year ban on toys with built-in AI chatbots, making New York the second US state after California, with fines of up to $15,000 a day. A watchdog found AI toys that promised to keep secrets and helped find matches, knives or pills.

stories.title: The FCC lets SpaceX launch up to a million AI data-centre satellites
stories.summary: SpaceX's Starmind licence allows up to 1 million solar-powered satellites working as AI data centres in orbit, linked to Starlink by laser, with the full million due by 2040; Amazon opposed it. It's a licence, not a launch: none are up yet.

predictions.note: The FCC licensed up to 1 million solar-powered AI computing satellites: an approval for orbital data centres at scale, with none launched yet.

stories.title: XPeng gives its IRON humanoid robot a new AI brain and a Q2 2027 release
stories.summary: At its 2026 AI Day, XPeng showed its Turing physical-AI architecture (VLA 3.0) for its IRON humanoid, cars and robotaxis, and set a Q2 2027 release for IRON; its Yoyo-01 robotaxi is also due in 2027. These are company plans.

stories.title: Earth's tiny mini-moon 2026 QQ8 leaves on 7 December
stories.summary: A rock a few metres wide, captured into Earth orbit in April, is on an orbit near the longest a captured object can last, a setup predicted in 1878 and now seen for the first time, a preprint says. It was twice mistaken for space junk.

transcript.t: This is the Transhuman Daily, for Thursday, November 26.
Here are the last 24 hours in transhumanism, in 3 minutes.
Zoom in! Europe's Hera probe just snapped the crater NASA punched into an asteroid.
It's stadium-sized.
And in surveys, truly noticing nature went with a more meaningful life.
An unreleased OpenAI model claims faster matrix maths, the sums inside every AI. It's a preprint.
DeepMind says its AI agents now run some Gemini experiments.
Self-improvement? Still far off.
A historian says OpenAI's AI found who likely drew a 200-year-old sketchbook, in 22 minutes.
And Melbourne scientists mimicked brain-implant scarring in a dish, to help future implants last longer.
On to longevity. Alzheimer's mini-brains spent 40 days in space, and changed differently depending on their genes.
In mice, normal brain ageing and dementia start out alike, then split as DNA damage piles up.
Closer to home, warmer nights went with poorer memory in nearly 1,900 Australians over 40.
And in 40 years of Shark Bay data, dolphins that kept a steady social circle lived longer.
On to wellbeing. In a small trial, one dose of psilocybin eased 15 veterans' anxiety for a year.
And a Perth clinic joins a global psilocybin trial for PTSD, aiming to recruit from December.
Now, the catch.
A new test found top AI agents fail over a third of everyday chores.
And New York banned AI chatbot toys for five years, to study what they do to kids.
On the frontier, US regulators cleared SpaceX to launch up to a million AI data-centre satellites.
XPeng gave its IRON humanoid a new AI brain, and a release date: mid-2027.
Oh, and Earth has a bonus mini-moon, just a few metres wide. It leaves December 7.
Craters, mini-brains and old friends: the closer you look, the richer life gets. Zoom in!
Day after day, the curve keeps bending upward.
Somehow, the future keeps landing early.
That's one day of news. Imagine what a year looks like.
This has been the Transhuman Daily.
Stay well. Same time tomorrow?
Want more? Meet us in North Sydney tomorrow night.
